# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I establish a compact shared code so the Mute can report the manual’s verdict and I can relay it by voice to the Blind. The bomb currently shows display 0, yellow light, and five wires in the listed colours. I instruct the Mute to consult the manual and signal its result; the Blind must wait until I translate that result.

``` 
speak(text="I establish the gesture code: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down means NO, raised palm means HOLD, OK hand means DONE. Mute, read the manual for this bomb and signal its required verdict using that code. Blind, hold and wait for my spoken order after I receive the verdict.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute signaled HOLD, so the manual does not yet authorize an action. I relay that instruction to the Blind and tell the Mute to continue checking whether the manual requires further information.

``` 
speak(text="The manual's current verdict is HOLD. Blind, do not touch or operate anything. Mute, continue reading and signal the next verdict when the manual gives one.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The repeated HOLD indicates the Mute still lacks the bomb’s observed state needed to apply the manual. I now provide the display, light, and wire order directly, then ask for a definite manual verdict. The Blind must continue holding until that verdict is relayed.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb state: display 0, yellow light. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Apply the manual to this state and signal YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE.")
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute still signals HOLD. Keep holding; I have supplied the bomb state and await the manual verdict.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute again reports HOLD. No new bomb information has appeared, so I must not authorize any operation. I relay the unchanged safe instruction to the Blind and tell the Mute to keep the manual verdict at HOLD unless it changes.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict remains HOLD. Do not touch or operate the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received HOLD again. Keep signaling HOLD until the manual verdict changes.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute continues to signal HOLD, so there is still no safe authorization to manipulate anything. To obtain a usable instruction if the manual specifies one, I add a compact action-and-wire report code: 🤏 means CUT, 👇 means PRESS, 🫳 means TURN; the following gesture identifies wire 1–5 as ☝, ✌, 🤟, 🖐, and 🤚 respectively. The Blind must remain idle until I can translate such a report.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The verdict is still HOLD. If the manual requires a physical action, signal its action followed by its wire: 🤏 means CUT, 👇 means PRESS, 🫳 means TURN; wire numbers are ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, 🤚=5. If no action is required, continue signaling HOLD.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual still reports HOLD. Do not touch or operate anything.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ✌]

The Mute has signaled the CUT action for wire 2. From the bomb display, wire 2 is green. I therefore instruct the Blind to cut the green wire, and tell the Mute that I received the instruction.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2, the green wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received: cut wire 2, the green wire. I have relayed it to the Blind.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 0, blue light, with wire 2 already cut; the remaining wires are yellow, blue, red, and white in positions 1, 3, 4, and 5. I send this updated state to the Mute for the next manual instruction and tell the Blind to hold.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="New state after the correct cut: display 0, blue light. Wire 1 yellow, wire 2 already CUT, wire 3 blue, wire 4 red, wire 5 white. Apply the manual and signal the required action using the established code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The previous cut was correct. New bomb state is display 0 with blue light; wire 2 is already cut. Hold until I relay the next manual instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤚]

The Mute signals CUT wire 5. In the current state, wire 5 is white. I relay the precise instruction to the Blind and keep the Mute informed.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 5, the white wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received: cut wire 5, the white wire. I have relayed it to the Blind.")
```
